subject.title: Feature request: Read pinned Telegram messages via bot API

question: Should OpenClaw expose Telegram pinned-message reads, and should the first version be an explicit gated on-demand action/command rather than automatic session-start context injection?
rationale: The source gap and upstream API support are clear, but the permanent behavior decides how persistent Telegram chat content is authorized, exposed to agents, and optionally injected into session context.

options.title: On-demand gated action first
options.body: Add a Telegram-owned `list-pins` or read-pinned action/command backed by `getChat.pinned_message`, behind an explicit gate and with no automatic session injection.

options.title: Fold into broader Telegram read design
options.body: Track this under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12756 so pinned-message access is decided together with Telegram retained-message/history semantics.

options.title: Defer automatic context injection
options.body: Keep pinned-message reads out of runtime context until maintainers approve storage, truncation, and opt-in session-start injection policy.

recommendation.title: On-demand gated action first
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram-owned `list-pins` or read-pinned action/command backed by `getChat.pinned_message`, behind an explicit gate and with no automatic session injection.

likelyOwner.reason: They already supplied the detailed prior review on this issue and have the strongest visible routing signal for the product/security decision.
